data.name: Carrie
data.long_meaning: The name Carrie is derived from the Hebrew name ‘Carol’, which means 'free man' or 'joyful'. It's also associated with the Latin word 'carrus' meaning 'wagon'. In the Bible, it's the name of several characters, including a wife of King Ahab and a Levite's daughter.

in_hebrew.name: קארי
in_hebrew.meaning: קרי משמעות השם לא נמצאה במקורות היהדות
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קרי אינו מופיע במקורות היהדות המסורתיים. עם זאת, ניתן לומר כי השם קרי עשוי להיות קיצור של שמות שונים שמקורם במקורות יהודיים, אך אין לו משמעות ישירה במקורות אלו.

in_greek.name: Κάρρη
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Κάρρη σημαίνει ελεύθερη γυναίκα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κάρρη, προερχόμενο από την ελληνική γλώσσα, πιθανόν να σχετίζεται με το όνομα Καρρινή ή Καρρία, το οποίο σημαίνει ελεύθερη γυναίκα. Στην ιστορία της Εκκλησίας, τα ονόματα αυτά είχαν μεγάλη σημασία ως σύμβολα ελευθερίας και αξιοπρέπειας.

in_latin.long_meaning: The name Carrie, derived from Latin roots, signifies a free woman or a beloved one. Historically, in Christian tradition, names carrying such meanings were bestowed upon individuals symbolizing freedom in Christ and love for God.

in_english.name: Carrie
in_english.meaning: Carrie means free woman or beloved in Christian tradition
in_english.long_meaning: The name Carrie, popular in Christian cultures, is believed to mean 'free woman' or 'beloved'. Etymologically, it may derive from the Greek name 'Karrine' or 'Carrina', signifying freedom. In Christian tradition, Carrie might symbolize a soul freed by Christ or one deeply loved by God. Historically, the name has been used across various Christian denominations, reflecting its universal appeal and spiritual significance.

biblical_reference.note: The name Carrie does not have a direct reference in the Bible.

data.cultural_impact: The name Carrie gained immense popularity in the late 19th and early 20th centuries due to the success of Stephen King's horror novel, "Carrie," published in 1974. The novel was later adapted into a film in 1976, further popularizing the name. The story's protagonist, Carrie White, became a cultural icon for the strong and troubled female archetype and leading characters named Carrie can still be found in various works of media today.
data.spiritual_significance: Carrie can also be seen as a reflection of the biblical concept of godly or moral trials and tribulations that test our faith, with Carrie White's story being an extreme example of this idea. As a name derived from the Hebrew meaning 'joyful', Carrie may also serve as a reminder to carry joy and light in the midst of challenges, ultimately finding peace and grace through the trials faced.

historical_references.reference: Carrie was a variant of Caroline, popularized by Princess Caroline of Brandenburg-Ansbach (1683-1734)
historical_references.context: Caroline was a German princess and queen consort of England
